# arubasdwan_bgp_config (Data Source)

Fetches the BGP configuration of the appliances from the Aruba SD-WAN Orchestrator: per appliance and VRF segment the system settings (local ASN, router ID, graceful restart, OSPF redistribution) and the configured neighbors (peer IP, remote ASN, peer type, timers, route policies, BFD). Appliances without BGP configuration are included with an empty VRF list.

The data is combined from these Orchestrator endpoints:

- `GET /gms/rest/appliance` — appliance inventory (hostname, serial, model, site)
- `GET /gms/rest/bgp/config/allVrfs/system` — BGP system configuration per appliance and VRF
- `GET /gms/rest/bgp/config/allVrfs/neighbor` — BGP neighbors per appliance and VRF

Orchestrator versions without the allVrfs endpoints fall back to the default-VRF endpoints `GET /gms/rest/bgp/config/system` and `GET /gms/rest/bgp/config/neighbor`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Read the BGP configuration of all appliances
data "arubasdwan_bgp_config" "all" {}

# BGP overview per appliance: local ASN, router ID, and peers per VRF
output "bgp" {
  value = {
    for a in data.arubasdwan_bgp_config.all.appliances :
    a.hostname => [
      for v in a.vrfs : {
        vrf       = v.vrf_name
        asn       = v.system.asn
        router_id = v.system.router_id
        enabled   = v.system.enabled
        peers = [
          for n in v.neighbors : {
            ip        = n.ip
            remote_as = n.remote_as
            type      = n.type
          }
        ]
      }
    ] if length(a.vrfs) > 0
  }
}

# All remote AS numbers peered with, e.g. for documentation exports
output "remote_as_numbers" {
  value = distinct(flatten([
    for a in data.arubasdwan_bgp_config.all.appliances : [
      for v in a.vrfs : [
        for n in v.neighbors : n.remote_as
      ]
    ]
  ]))
}

# Read a single appliance by its Orchestrator primary key
data "arubasdwan_bgp_config" "branch01" {
  ne_pk = "3.NE"
}

# Server-side filtering: exclude lab systems, restrict to one site.
# Filtered appliances are never queried.
data "arubasdwan_bgp_config" "filtered" {
  exclude_hostname_regex = "(?i)^(lab|test)-"
  sites                  = ["Berlin"]
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `cached` (Boolean) Whether to read BGP data from the Orchestrator database (true, default) or live from each appliance (false). Live reads are slower and fail for unreachable appliances.
- `exclude_hostname_regex` (String) Exclude appliances whose hostname matches this RE2 regular expression (e.g. "(?i)^(lab|test)-").
- `exclude_models` (List of String) Exclude appliances whose model is in this list (case-insensitive exact match, e.g. ["EC-V"]).
- `exclude_sites` (List of String) Exclude appliances whose site is in this list (case-insensitive exact match).
- `hostname_regex` (String) Only include appliances whose hostname matches this RE2 regular expression (e.g. "^br-" or "(?i)^(ber|ham)-").
- `models` (List of String) Only include appliances whose model is in this list (case-insensitive exact match, e.g. ["EC-S-B"]). Filters apply before any per-appliance data is fetched.
- `ne_pk` (String) Optional appliance primary key (e.g. "3.NE") to fetch a single appliance. If omitted, all appliances are returned.
- `sites` (List of String) Only include appliances whose site is in this list (case-insensitive exact match).

All filters are combined with AND and applied before any per-appliance data is fetched, so excluded appliances are never queried.

### Read-Only

- `appliances` (Attributes List) List of appliances with their per-VRF BGP configuration, sorted by hostname. Appliances without BGP configuration carry an empty vrfs list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances))

<a id="nestedatt--appliances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances`

Read-Only:

- `hostname` (String) Hostname of the appliance.
- `model` (String) Appliance model (e.g. "EC-S-B").
- `ne_pk` (String) Orchestrator primary key of the appliance (e.g. "3.NE").
- `serial` (String) Hardware serial number of the appliance.
- `site` (String) Site name the appliance is tagged with in the Orchestrator.
- `vrfs` (Attributes List) BGP configuration per VRF segment, sorted by VRF ID; empty if the appliance has no BGP configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--vrfs))

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--vrfs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.vrfs`

Read-Only:

- `neighbors` (Attributes List) BGP neighbors configured in the VRF segment, sorted by peer IP address; empty if none are configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--vrfs--neighbors))
- `system` (Attributes) BGP system (process) configuration of the VRF segment. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--appliances--vrfs--system))
- `vrf_id` (Number) VRF segment ID the configuration belongs to (0 = Default).
- `vrf_name` (String) Resolved VRF segment name (e.g. "Default"); empty if it cannot be resolved.

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--vrfs--neighbors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.vrfs.neighbors`

Read-Only:

- `as_prepend_count` (Number) Number of additional times the local AS is prepended to the AS path.
- `bfd_enabled` (Boolean) True if a BFD session is desired for this peer.
- `directly_connected` (Boolean) True if the peer adjacency is treated as single hop, false for multi hop.
- `enabled` (Boolean) True if the BGP session to this neighbor is enabled.
- `evpn` (Boolean) True if EVPN is enabled for this peer.
- `export_map` (Number) Route export policies bitmask; 4294967295 means the predefined bitmask of the peer type is unchanged.
- `hold_timer` (Number) Hold timer in seconds: how long to wait for a KEEPALIVE or UPDATE message before the neighbor is considered dead.
- `import_routes` (Boolean) True if routes learned from the neighbor are imported.
- `inbound_med` (Number) Metric applied to routes received from the neighbor.
- `ip` (String) IP address of the neighbor.
- `keepalive_timer` (Number) Interval in seconds between KEEPALIVE messages to the neighbor.
- `local_preference` (Number) Local preference for routes advertised to the neighbor.
- `med` (Number) Multi-Exit Discriminator for routes advertised to the neighbor.
- `next_hop_self` (Boolean) True if the appliance advertises its own IP address as next hop.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) MD5 password of the BGP session; may be empty or masked by the Orchestrator.
- `remote_as` (Number) Remote autonomous system number of the neighbor (4-byte ASNs supported).
- `type` (String) Peer type of the neighbor (e.g. "Branch", "Branch-transit", "PE-router").

<a id="nestedatt--appliances--vrfs--system"></a>
### Nested Schema for `appliances.vrfs.system`

Read-Only:

- `asn` (Number) Local autonomous system number (4-byte ASNs supported).
- `enabled` (Boolean) True if BGP is enabled in this VRF segment.
- `graceful_restart` (Boolean) True if graceful restart is enabled.
- `max_restart_time` (Number) Maximum time in seconds to wait for a restarting peer before its advertised routes are removed from the routing tables (1-3600).
- `redistribute_ospf` (Boolean) True if BGP routes are redistributed to OSPF.
- `redistribute_ospf_filter` (Number) Filter bitmask applied to routes redistributed to OSPF.
- `remote_as_path_advertise` (Boolean) True if the remote AS path is propagated when advertising routes.
- `router_id` (String) BGP router ID.
- `stale_path_time` (Number) Maximum time in seconds stale routes of a restarted peer are kept before removal (1-3600).
